ideas.statement: An old watch repairer whose market stall is closing helps a young courier, Mei, mend her grandmother's watch herself.

elements.label: Mr Lo, a repairer whose stall is closing
Mei repairs her grandmother's watch with his help

evidence.quote: the market would close on Friday
guided her hands while she lifted out the broken wheel

questions.opening: What is this story mainly about?

focus.E1: Who is Mr Lo, and what is happening to his stall?
focus.E2: What does Mei end up doing with the broken watch?

questions.clarify: Can you say a little more, using the story?

ideas.statement: Mei needs the watch working for her sister's wedding on Saturday, but Mr Lo refuses because his stall closes on Friday.

elements.label: Mei wants it for the Saturday wedding
Mr Lo refuses: no stall left to finish the work

evidence.quote: Her sister was getting married on Saturday, and Mei wanted her to wear it
by Friday there would be no stall to finish it at

questions.opening: What problem stands between Mei and her plan for the watch?

focus.E1: Why does Mei want the watch fixed this week?
focus.E2: Why does Mr Lo refuse to open the watch?

questions.clarify: Which part of the story are you thinking of?

ideas.statement: Mr Lo changes his mind after Mei shows she has taught herself about watch parts, which reminds him of how he learned.

elements.label: Mei shows she taught herself about the parts
Mr Lo agrees to help after all

relation.direction: Mei's self-taught knowledge, so like his own way of learning, leads Mr Lo to help

evidence.quote: asked whether the one with the missing tooth was the escape wheel
He had learned the same way
On Thursday he unwrapped the biscuit tin

questions.opening: What makes Mr Lo change his mind about the watch?

focus.E1: What does Mei ask about the tray of tiny wheels?
focus.E2: What does Mr Lo do with the biscuit tin on Thursday?

questions.link: How is Mei's way of learning connected to Mr Lo's own past?
questions.clarify: Which part of the story are you thinking of?

ideas.statement: Mr Lo does not fix the watch himself; he guides Mei's hands while she replaces the broken wheel.

elements.label: he guides instead of repairing it himself

evidence.quote: He did not repair the watch
fitted the one he had kept in a matchbox for twenty years

questions.opening: Who actually does the repair work on Thursday?

focus.E1: What is Mr Lo's part in the repair?
focus.E2: What does Mei herself do to the watch?

questions.clarify: Which part of the story are you thinking of?

ideas.statement: The watch works but runs two minutes slow; Mr Lo gives Mei his loupe and says it is close enough for the wedding.

elements.label: the watch ticks but loses two minutes a day
Mr Lo gives Mei his loupe

evidence.quote: It lost about two minutes a day
Mr Lo pressed the loupe into her hand

questions.opening: How do things stand when Mei leaves the market on Friday?

focus.E1: How well does the watch keep time in the end?
focus.E2: What does Mr Lo give Mei before she goes?
